turns.t: Morning, doctor. Sorry, I know it's probably nothing, but these headaches are really doing my head in.
No need to apologise. Tell me what they're like.
It's mostly across the front, like a tight band, and it creeps in around mid-afternoon.
And how long has that been going on?
Um, about two weeks now. Maybe a bit more, I'm not really counting.
Is it there all day, or does it come and go?
It comes and goes, but most days it shows up once I've been staring at the screen for a few hours.
So screens seem to bring it on. Does anything ease it?
A glass of water and stepping outside helps a bit. Not much else I've tried, really.
How bad does it get, if you had to put a word on it?
Moderate, I'd say. It's annoying more than anything. I can still work, just slower.
Any sickness, flashing lights or trouble with your vision when it's there?
No, nothing like that. No sickness, and my eyes feel okay, apart from being a bit tired by the evening.
Have you had a knock to the head recently, or a fall?
No, nothing like that.
How's your sleep been lately?
Not brilliant, to be honest. I've been going to bed late because of a deadline. Five hours a night, maybe.
That alone can do it. And how much caffeine are you getting through?
Three or four coffees, I'd say. More when the deadline is close.
Okay. I'll have a look at your eyes, and feel your neck and temples, if that's alright?
Sure, go ahead.
Your neck moves freely, there's no tenderness over the temples, and your eyes follow my finger normally. Nothing worrying there.
Good. So what's causing it, do you think?
From what you've told me this looks like a tension-type headache, the sort that builds with screen time, short sleep and plenty of coffee. I'm not seeing anything pointing to something more serious.
That's a relief. I was starting to google brain tumours at midnight.
Please don't do that to yourself. Let's try the simple things first.
Like what?
Look away from the screen every hour, drink water through the day, cut the coffee down to one or two, and aim for seven hours of sleep.
Seven hours sounds optimistic, but I'll try.
Give it a couple of weeks. If it's not better in two weeks, come back and see me and we'll think again.
And if it suddenly gets worse?
Then don't wait. A sudden severe headache, vomiting, or any weakness or trouble speaking means come straight in or call for help.
Understood. Thank you, I feel much better about it.
Good. Look after yourself, and try to rest that deadline brain a little.
I'll do my best. Bye, doctor.
Bye now.
